title: Ext vanishing makes the final kernel of an injective resolution injective
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $N$ an $R$-module, in a common universe. Let $I^\bullet$ be an integer-indexed cochain complex and $\varepsilon:N\to I^0$ an $R$-linear map such that $I^j=0$ for $j<0$, every $I^j$ is injective, and $0\to N\xrightarrow{\varepsilon}I^0\xrightarrow{\partial^0}I^1\to\cdots$ is exact [def-sp-injective-resolutions, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Fix an integer $d\geq0$ and put $J=\ker(\partial^d:I^d\to I^{d+1})$. Suppose that $\operatorname{Ext}^{d+1}_R(R/T,N)=0$ for every ideal $T\subseteq R$, with Ext defined in [def-pc-ext]. Then $J$ is an injective $R$-module.

source.place: Tag 0A5T, lemma-injective-amplitude, proof of (3) implies (1), final-kernel injectivity and truncation.

proof.text: Work in the abelian category $\operatorname{Mod}(R)$, whose monomorphisms are the injective linear maps by [lem-weil-pbc-ring-modules-enough-injectives]. Fix an ideal $T\subseteq R$ and a linear map $f:T\to J$, and write $\iota:J\hookrightarrow I^d$ for the kernel inclusion. Since $I^d$ is injective, the extension property in [def-sp-injective-resolutions], applied to $T\hookrightarrow R$ and $\iota f$, gives $a:R\to I^d$ with $a|_T=\iota f$.

source.place: Tag 0A5T, lemma-injective-amplitude, proof of (3) implies (1), final-kernel injectivity; expanded by the ideal-extension test of Tag 0AVF, lemma-characterize-injective-bis.

proof.text: Let $q:R\twoheadrightarrow R/T$ be the quotient map. Because $\partial^d a(t)=\partial^d\iota f(t)=0$ for $t\in T$, the formula $\alpha(r+T)=\partial^d a(r)$ defines a well-defined linear map $\alpha:R/T\to I^{d+1}$ with $\alpha q=\partial^d a$. It is a cocycle: for every $r\in R$, $\partial^{d+1}\alpha(r+T)=\partial^{d+1}\partial^d a(r)=0$ by the cochain-complex identity.

source.place: Tag 0A5T, lemma-injective-amplitude, proof of (3) implies (1), final-kernel injectivity; expanded by the ideal-extension test of Tag 0AVF, lemma-characterize-injective-bis.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ext-via-injective-resolution] to the given augmented resolution of $N$, with first argument $R/T$ and degree $d+1>0$. Its hypotheses hold because the given complex is nonnegative, degreewise injective, and augmented exact, in the abelian module category of step 1. The assumed vanishing of $\operatorname{Ext}^{d+1}_R(R/T,N)$ makes $H^{d+1}(\operatorname{Hom}_R(R/T,I^\bullet))$ zero. The explicit cocycle-modulo-boundaries formula in the cited statement therefore supplies $b:R/T\to I^d$ satisfying $\partial^d b=\alpha$.

source.place: Tag 06XR, lemma-compute-ext-resolutions, (1), for the two modules in degree zero; cochain homotopies identify boundaries.

proof.text: Put $h=a-bq:R\to I^d$. Then $\partial^d h=\partial^d a-(\partial^d b)q=\alpha q-\alpha q=0$, so $\widetilde f(r)=h(r)$, regarded as an element of the kernel $J$, is linear. For $t\in T$, $q(t)=0$ gives $h(t)=a(t)=\iota f(t)$, hence $\widetilde f|_T=f$. This constructs an extension to $R$ of the arbitrary map $f:T\to J$.

source.place: Tag 0A5T, lemma-injective-amplitude, proof of (3) implies (1), final-kernel injectivity; expanded by the ideal-extension test of Tag 0AVF, lemma-characterize-injective-bis.

proof.text: Every linear map from every ideal of $R$ into $J$ thus extends to $R$. Apply [lem-sf-baer-criterion] with $A=R$ and this module $J$: its ideal-extension condition implies that $J$ is injective. The common-universe hypothesis is exactly the one in that criterion.
